per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window in loop DE. Free WT SSB-2 (12-224) at 22 °C, pH 7.0, 600 MHz has loop DE I135-E165 (entry 130-160) at S2 0.67 ± 0.16 (SPRY-J1, r1); the core (0.93), loop FG and the six observable loop-CD amides (0.89) are ordered (J2, measured_not_detected). Normal modes of the apo structure also put the largest fluctuations in loops CD and DE (J7, md_only). The first 500 MHz data set failed for short R1 delays (J6, artefact_suspected).
per_window.us-ms: Qualitative only. Seven loop-CD amides H119-G125 (entry 114-120) are absent at 5-22 °C and 500-800 MHz and CLEANEX recovers none, which the authors attribute to intermediate exchange (J4, r3-r6, indirect). Among observable amides, 15N CPMG at 600 MHz, 22 °C (20-1000 Hz) shows no dispersion (J3, r2); apparent Modelfree Rex terms are treated as possible tensor bias (J5, artefact_suspected). No kex, population or delta omega exists.
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient (J16). No H/D exchange or slower process is in the rows.
per_window.undetermined: Homolog normal modes (J8, GUSTAVUS and PRYSPRY), crystal versus solution comparison (J9, abstract only), Par-4-bound CSP (J10), VASA-bound human crystal versus apo mouse crystal (J11), binding kinetics of iNOS, RGD and TAT peptides to human SPSB2 (J12-J14) and MD of a docked human complex (J15). Not judged: r12, r17, r18, r20, r31 (19F/SPR binding of ligands, abstracts), r13, r19, r27, r34, r35 (ligand conformations in human complex crystals), r14 (NMR structure abstract), r25, r26 (unassigned CSPs), r28, r29 (NanoBRET target engagement), r30, r33 (affinity only).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Qualitatively, at one site and without rate or population: in free WT murine SSB-2 (12-224) at 22 °C, pH 7.0 (phosphate/EDTA) the seven loop-CD amides H119-G125 (entry 114-120) stay missing at 5-22 °C and 500-800 MHz, which the authors attribute to intermediate-timescale exchange, while 15N CPMG (600 MHz, 20-1000 Hz) shows no dispersion in any observable amide.
open_conflicts: Apparent Modelfree Rex terms in the 600 MHz relaxation fit (r1) versus flat CPMG dispersion at 20-1000 Hz (r2); the authors attribute the Rex terms to possible diffusion-tensor bias, which is plausible but not tested.
questions_for_gina: Should the loop-CD amides missing at every tested temperature and field (with a CLEANEX control but no dispersion) count as WT apo µs-ms detection, as done here with indirect strength?
The input card gives no BMRB id; is the RelaxDB SPRY set the 600 MHz, 22 °C relaxation data of Yao et al. 2006 (doi:10.1110/ps.062477806)?
protein_summary.buffer_note: All murine SSB-2 NMR samples are in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, pH 7.0 (pH 6.7 for the Par-4 titration); no phosphate or EDTA effect is shown, so no row is marked artefact for buffer. The construct precipitates above 22 °C or below pH 6.5, which limited the temperature series. Human SPSB2 rows (SPR, CSP, crystals, MD, NanoBRET) are a different species and construct and never set a mouse verdict. Second read flagged r1 (residue list, corrected in the CSV to A111-D118, S126-S128, I135-E165, G183-L199); the corrected list still mixes the flexible loop DE with the ordered loops CD and FG, so J1 uses loop DE only.

detection.method: 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion, in-phase/anti-phase coherence-averaged R2app, constant 40 ms CPMG segment
detection.detection_window: One field (600 MHz), 22 °C, nuCPMG 20-1000 Hz, 40 ms relaxation delay: exchange refocused within this range and large enough to rise above the R2app scatter would show; exchange too fast to be refocused at 1000 Hz, too small to stand out, or at the unobserved H119-G125 amides would not.

judgments.reason: R2app fluctuates but shows no significant, consistent change with CPMG field, so the authors find no submillisecond-to-millisecond exchange in the observable amides under these conditions; no rate bound or population is given.

judgments.reason: Seven loop-CD amides never appear at any tested temperature or field, and CLEANEX recovers no peaks, which argues against fast solvent exchange; the authors therefore attribute their absence to intermediate-timescale conformational exchange, with no rate, population or delta omega.
judgments.function_link: The authors suggest loop CD may adopt multiple conformations relative to the beta-sandwich core; no binding role is measured.
